analysis: All five units are documentation-only changes. docs/developer/build.md gets a date bump plus CI runner-routing prose. Only the later tail of the file (head lines 897-1129) was supplied, and it appears to be unchanged surrounding text about build, verify and qualification guidance. docs/developer/desktop-app.md (patch hunk at head lines 331-337) now says manual dispatch of desktop.yml runs a `desktop-package` job. That job produces the unsigned `unsigned-desktop-review` artifact on a Darkbloom Sandbox Mac when the plane grants one, and otherwise on `blacksmith-12vcpu-macos-27`. The doc states it does not publish a release or establish attestation qualification. No code, provider keys, attestation paths, coordinator-provider protocol, cache storage or privileged helpers change. I found no new attack surface or regression against the threat model (TB-011 qualification, T-054, T-041 and others). One thing the next pass could check: the CI change routes jobs to Darkbloom Sandbox Macs (TB-012/TB-013 territory, T-061). The workflow YAML and runner-routing implementation are not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot assess whether the unsigned desktop-package artifact, or any secrets exposed to that routed runner, create supply-chain risk. That is an unverified contract, not a finding. Docs claims about CSC signing and unsigned review builds look consistent with the existing text (desktop-app.md base lines 83-85).
